text:
jen_support: Heads-up: customer 'NeonPay' reporting spike of 503s + intermittent auth failures when requests should route to eu-central-1 but end up in us-west. Billing shows retries counting against their quota — need triage.
sam_sre: can you paste the request/response headers and any envoy access logs? tx
jen_support: pasted curl + response headers below:
```bash
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" -H \"x-redwood-region: eu-central-1\" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
server: envoy
x-redwood-region: us-west-2
x-request-id: 0a12b3f4
content-type: application/json
```
Envoy access log (snippet):
```
[2026-03-17T09:01:12.123Z] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 503 - 0 0 12 9 "-" "curl/7.85.0" "10.10.5.12" "upstream_cluster:\"fallback-cluster-us\" upstream_host:\"10.20.30.5:443\""
```
lee_eng: that log is telling — request had x-redwood-region set to eu but upstream_cluster is fallback-cluster-us. my hunch: the L7 route fallback path is rewriting/preserving headers incorrectly when it chooses the fallback cluster. maybe recent route config uses header insertion with append instead of replace so x-redwood-region gets overridden. can you also confirm who deployed route config?

opsbot: deploy-bot: route-config v2 rolled to prod at 1995120285 by @infra_jam :information_source:

jen_support: infra_jam did the rollout ~4m before first reports. i reproduced locally by forcing unavailable cluster for eu and saw header flip. Repro steps i used:

```
# force fallback: set env var on test proxy
curl -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/test/proxy/control\" -d '{"fail_eu":true}'
# then send request
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" -H \"x-redwood-region: eu-central-1\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# observe x-redwood-region in response becomes us-west-2 and 503
```
jamal_sre: temporary mitigation suggestion: set the edge route to preserve x-redwood-region (header_preserve true) or add an immediate header replace action to prefer incoming header over cluster default. we can also roll back route-config v2 if infra approves. i'll prepare rollback patch now. :clock10:

lee_eng: agree with rollback as quick mitigation. long-term fix: change route header action to `replace` and ensure cluster selection does not inject region header after route decision. i'll open PR in eng-runtime and link tests. ETA 2-4h for PR + canary.

maria_sa: customer marked this sev2 and flagged billing impact — can we confirm rollback and send brief to customer PM? they want ETA and temporary credit if retries cause overage. :phone:

jen_support: created support ticket SUP-8932, notified customer, and asked for credit eval. jamal, pls push rollback and update thread. will keep customer posted. :white_check_mark:
